evidence.quote:
All data manipulation and construction of the datasets for analyses was done using SAS. The final
   analyses were conducted using a combination of SAS and Stata. A further description of the sample
   construction and definition of variables can be found in Section 3, the appendix, and the online
   appendix of the manuscript. We also provide code to fulfill JAR's Data and Code Sharing Policy.
   Specifically, we include the following program files used in the assembly of the various datasets
   for analysis and the program file used to generate the main results.
       •   BDEM_1_Data_Assembly_Code_SAS.sas: The SAS program that produces the main
           dataset used as an input in other programs or to create additional datasets after processing.
       •   BDEM_2_Add_Var_Creation_STATA.do: The Stata code used to create additional
           relevant variables for the main analysis.
       •   BDEM_3_Main_Tables_STATA.do: The Stata code used to generate the main results.
       •   BDEM_ICO_Identifiers.xls: The file with names for the final sample of 2,113 ICOs in our
           final sample.

evidence.quote:
•   To convert the amount of funds raised during the ICO in US Dollar terms, we collected Bitcoin
    and Ethereum exchange rates against the US Dollar from Datastream.
•   Price data (open, close, low, high) and token volume data from coinmarketcap.com were
    collected on May 15, 2018 and were updated on October 25, 2018. Coinmarketcap.com
    provides weekly historical snapshots of all coins and tokens in its coverage universe. We
    manually downloaded 66 month-end snapshots from April, 2013 to October, 2018 available
    from here: https://coinmarketcap.com/historical/. From these snapshots, we identified tokens
    for our sample by using a tag that is available on the detailed page for each token (i.e., a token
    flag similar to a stock ticker). Price data for all tokens were then scraped using a Python web
    scraping script. This process ensures that we capture all tokens that have ever been covered by
    coinmarketcap.com. We compare the two vintages of the data (May 15, 2018 and October 25,
    2018), and find that the overlapping price data are exactly the same, which gives us comfort
evidence.description: The datasheet describes historical Datastream BTC/ETH exchange rates and CoinMarketCap market-price collection; the broad public-source statement does not resolve Datastream terms or current compatibility.
The SAS preparation constructs daily leads/lags, forward returns, and liquidity measures. Preserve its exact close-condition syntax.

/* Merge in CMC daily market data to the cleaned ICO-level "Names" file **/

	create table coinmarketcap7 as select

	a.name_coinschedule, a.name_tokendata, a.name_icorating, a.name_smith_crown,

	on a.url_cmc=b.url
	order by a.combined_name, b.date;

evidence.quote:
** Generate Disclosure Index
	gen tdisc = (wp_UOP + wp_norm + github_sourcecode + wp_tech_whitepaper + wp_product_roadmap_info + team_identity + wp_token_dist_ftap_ind + wp_vesting_ind + video_presentation + social_media_presence) 
	egen tdisc_r = xtile(tdisc), n(10)
	sum tdisc_r, d
	gen tdisc_norm = (tdisc_r - `r(min)') / (`r(max)'-`r(min)')
	label var tdisc_norm "Disclosure Index"


	** Generate Disclosure Index (without vesting & insider tokens disclosure - for cross-sectional tests)
	gen tdisc3 = (wp_UOP + wp_norm + github_sourcecode + wp_tech_whitepaper + wp_product_roadmap_info + team_identity + video_presentation + social_media_presence) 
	egen tdisc3_r = xtile(tdisc3), n(10)
	sum tdisc3_r, d
	gen tdisc3_norm = (tdisc3_r - `r(min)') / (`r(max)'-`r(min)')
	label var tdisc3_norm "Disclosure Index - exc. FTAP & vesting"

	** Prinicpal Components of Disclosure measures
	pca wp_UOP wp_norm github_sourcecode wp_tech_whitepaper wp_product_roadmap_info team_identity wp_token_dist_ftap_ind  wp_vesting_ind video_presentation social_media_presence, mineigen(1) 
	predict pc1 pc2

** Create "Size" control variable (using multiple sources)
	gen mv_raw1 = mv_mm*1000000
	gen mv_raw2 = total_supply_coinmarketcap*close*1000000
	gen mv_raw3 = total_supply_coinmarketcap*close_lag1*1000000
	gen mv_raw4 = total_supply_coinmarketcap*ico_price*1000000
	gen total_sold = tokens_for_sale_icobench*ico_price
	gen total_supply_usd2 = total_supply_usd*1000000
	egen size_temp = rowfirst(mv_raw1 mv_raw2 mv_raw3 mv_raw4 soft_cap_usd_icobench hard_cap_usd_icobench total_sold total_supply_usd2)
	gen size = ln(1+size_temp)

	save dataset_for_analysis, replace

*** Create fixed effects and clustering variables
encode Industry_FE_desc, gen(industry_f)
encode region, gen(region_f)

evidence.quote:
The following rawdata files are used to construct our main sample: 

	1. rawdata.coinmarketcap: This data file contains daily price, volume, marekt cap, token identifiers, and website 
	information for listed tokens (active and inactive) from Coin Market Cap (https://coinmarketcap.com). 
	2. rawdata.names: This file contains a linking table (manually created) allowing us to merge ICO information from 
	various data sources based on token name, given token names appear to vary slightly across datasets.
	3. rawdata.icobench: This file contains various ICO information collected/downloaded from ICOBench (https://icobench.com/).				
	4. rawdata.icorating: This file contains various ICO information collected/downloaded from ICORating (https://icorating.com/).
	5. rawdata.smithandcrown: This file contains various ICO information downloaded from Smith & Crown (https://smithandcrown.com/)
	6. rawdata.tokendata: This file contains various ICO information collected from Token Data (https://research.tokendata.io/).
	7. rawdata.coinschedule: This file contains various ICO information (primarily ICO start/end dates) collected from Coin Schedule.
	8. rawdata.Benchy: This files contains detailed information on ICO Ratings and ICO analysts, collected from ICOBench (https://icobench.com/).	
	9. rawdata.wpc_allvars_20190320: This file contains information collected directly from white papers (coded by co-author team).
evidence.description: The supplied SAS header enumerates the rawdata files and describes the CoinMarketCap panel, manually constructed Names link table, aggregator/rating data, Benchy data, and team-coded rated whitepaper variables.
SAS reads daily CoinMarketCap and Names inputs, keeps rows with url_cmc, and links the panel on url=url_cmc.
The Names input is filtered by combined_drop, drops secid/icoid, de-duplicates combined_name and supplies the cross-source names and end-date fields used in the CMC merge.
